evidence.description: Each digester is collapsed to a single across-session mean before any inferential procedure, yielding exactly one analysed value per independent vessel.

source_refs.quoted_text:
def digester_table(sessions):
    """One analysed row per independent vessel: its across-session mean yield."""
    table = []
    for unit in sorted(sessions):
        arm, yields = sessions[unit]
        table.append((unit, arm, len(yields), float(np.mean(yields))))
    return table

evidence.description: The Mann-Whitney U test is applied to the arm-wise arrays drawn from the vessel-level table (6 thermal means vs 6 control means), not to the 48 raw session rows.

def arm_values(table, arm):

evidence.description: The reported test statistics are numerically consistent only with a 6-vs-6 vessel-level test: U = 36.0 is the maximum attainable with n1 = n2 = 6 (6*6 = 36), and the exact two-sided p = 0.002165 equals 2/C(12,6) = 2/924, the value for complete separation of the two sets of six vessel means. A row-level test on 48 records could not produce these values (max U would be 24*24 = 576).

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the no-issue verdict by checking whether the reported statistics could actually stem from a hidden row-level (n = 48) analysis despite the vessel-level prose. Recomputation shows they cannot: (1) all 12 reported digester means reproduce exactly from the raw CSV session rows; (2) the six thermal vessel means (283.3-318.4) completely separate from the six control vessel means (239.5-271.4), for which the exact two-sided Mann-Whitney p is 2/C(12,6) = 2/924 = 0.0021645, matching the reported 0.002165, and U = 36.0 is exactly the 6x6 maximum; a 24-vs-24 row-level test would have a maximum U of 576 and, given the same complete separation in the raw rows, a far smaller p-value. (3) Code inspection confirms mannwhitneyu receives only the arm_values arrays built from the one-row-per-digester table, and no code path passes session-level rows to any inferential procedure. I also checked read_sessions for grouping errors (e.g., unit keys not stripped, or arm reassignment across rows) and found none; each digester_id maps to one arm and one mean.
